blinding_guess.why: For ROS 2 array-typed fields the JSON list is assigned unchanged (message_conversion.py:361-362); a sensor_msgs/Joy.axes list arriving from JSON with integral values (0, 1, -1) would not be converted to float before being set on a float32 sequence, so Joy.axes looks likely to be rejected by the generated message setter. The QoS peer-matching is taken once at subscription time, which could also leave a reliable subscriber against a later best-effort mavros publisher.

notes: rosbridge_suite 1.2.0 is a generic JSON/WebSocket bridge. None of the six packet elements is named anywhere in the snapshot (case-insensitive grep for joy, mavros, global_position, local_position, axes, buttons: 0 hits). Topic names, message types and fields all arrive at run time from client JSON (subscribe.py:243/275, publish.py:62) or from graph discovery (subscribers.py:79-94 uses get_topic_names_and_types when the client gives no type), so references, declares and not_declared are empty (all packet elements are consumed and none is named in code). Ports are recorded for all six elements because the subscribe/publish code path would carry them, but every identity field the code does not fix is null. msg_type of the msg/field ports is the parent type named by the element itself (the loader accepts 'sensor_msgs/Joy' or 'sensor_msgs/msg/Joy', ros_loader.py:176-187; internally the code compares 'pkg/msg/Type' strings, message_conversion.py:192-198); msg_type of the two topic ports is null (client-supplied or discovered). definition_id is null everywhere: the package pins no definition and loads whatever sensor_msgs is installed via importlib (ros_loader.py:165-171); sensor_msgs is only a test_depend, so no dependency definition was fetched. QoS (subscriber path, subscribers.py:111-121): base QoSProfile(depth=10, durability=VOLATILE, reliability=RELIABLE), then durability becomes TRANSIENT_LOCAL if any currently discovered publisher on the topic is TRANSIENT_LOCAL and reliability becomes BEST_EFFORT if any currently discovered publisher is BEST_EFFORT (get_publishers_info_by_topic at subscription time; publishers appearing later are not re-matched). Because reliability and durability are selected from discovered peers' profiles they are recorded null. No deadline, lifespan or liveliness is set on the subscriber; deadline_ms null (code sets none; no in-snapshot citation for the rclpy default). If instead rosbridge publishes on a client-named topic (publishers.py:106-119) it fixes durability TRANSIENT_LOCAL, depth=queue_size (client, default 100; 1 when latched) and lifespan 1 s when not latched; reliability is not set there. rate_hz null: throttle_rate/queue_length are per-client JSON fields (subscribe.py:276-278). frame/units null: the bridge never interprets headers or units. Field handling: fields are walked generically (message_conversion.py:266, 384-397); for a std_msgs/Header field inst.stamp is overwritten with ROSClock().now() before the client's values are applied (message_conversion.py:381-382); for array-typed ROS 2 fields (array.array / numpy, e.g. float32[] axes, int32[] buttons) the incoming JSON list is returned unchanged with no element conversion (message_conversion.py:361-362), whereas scalar ints are cast to float for float fields (message_conversion.py:334-337). Outgoing float lists map NaN/Inf to null (message_conversion.py:216-220). perm_grants lists the three glob allowlist parameters as named in code; their declared defaults are the empty string, which disables filtering. exclusive is empty: the only exclusively bound resource is the WebSocket listen socket (port parameter, default 9090, rosbridge_websocket.py:110/150), not a hardware or device handle. The node also publishes client_count (std_msgs/Int32, TRANSIENT_LOCAL) which is not a packet element.
